candidates.priorities_note: His website's "Priorities" page had only placeholder text ("lorem ipsum") when we checked on Oct 9, 2026, so there was no list of issues to use.

cost-of-living.heading: Making Life More Affordable
cost-of-living.quote: As a former Department of Revenue Director and Budget Director, Kurt balanced budgets to limit inflation and cut taxes to put money back into the pockets of Montanans – to make life more affordable.

candidates.priorities_note: His Platform page opens with a letter that calls cutting federal money to Montana's Department of Labor and Industry his "number one priority," so that is listed first, followed by the first two items on his platform list.

priorities.heading: My fellow Montanans
priorities.quote: As a candidate for the United States Senate, it is my number one priority when elected to pull the roughly $66.9 million federal dollars that is provided to the DLI. Doing so will downsize the big government, reduce taxes, create economic stability, and allow small businesses to thrive once more in our great State of Montana.

priorities.heading: Agriculture
priorities.quote: When elected to the United States Senate, Austin will work hard to overhaul the USDA and agriculture programs. This will include 0% financing for all ag producers and infrastructure improvements such as railways, highways and fertilizer production facility in the United States.

priorities.heading: 2nd Amendment
priorities.quote: Austin believes everyone American should un-restricted access to bear arms.

health-care.heading: Healthcare 2.0
health-care.quote: Austin has plans, when elected, to overhaul our healthcare system to improve access and quality to all United States citizens.

priorities.heading: Affordability
priorities.quote: Bring the cost of living back to earth: housing, groceries, and care a Montana paycheck can actually cover.

priorities.heading: Accountability
priorities.quote: Zero corporate PAC money. Show up, answer for the work, and put Montana ahead of donors and special interests, the way service taught her.

priorities.heading: Protecting the Vulnerable
priorities.quote: A career spent on crimes against children, brought to the Senate, and a fierce guard for those most easily overlooked.

cost-of-living.heading: Jobs & Wages
cost-of-living.quote: Raise the federal minimum wage to at least $17 an hour by 2030, so a full-time job keeps a worker and their family out of poverty, and index it to inflation the way Montana already does, so the floor never sits frozen for 17 years again.

housing.heading: Housing
housing.quote: Tax breaks for builders who make at least 30% of their units genuinely affordable.
housing.note: Her housing plan also backs the HOPE for Homeownership Act and down-payment help for first-time buyers. Those passages are longer than our 60-word limit, so see her Positions page for the full plan.

health-care.heading: Healthcare
health-care.quote: I’m a universal healthcare girl. If you have a medical emergency, your focus should be getting better, not wondering if you’re about to go bankrupt.

immigration.heading: Immigration & Border Security
immigration.quote: You shut it down, and the name ICE goes with it, because that name now stands for something that has no place in this country. You account for exactly how it got this bad, and you build its replacement from scratch, into whatever organizational solution an honest, independent review recommends.

foreign-policy.heading: Iran
foreign-policy.quote: Vote to end the war and invoke the War Powers Resolution to bring our troops home, since Congress never authorized this.

climate-energy.heading: Energy
climate-energy.quote: Expand real choice, never mandates: bring back the home solar and battery credits families used to get, and the EV-charging credit, so any Montanan who wants to add them gets help doing it.
